research_goal: Create backend-ready kickboxing strike mechanics, combinations, entries, exits, kick defense, and countering knowledge for SFTC.

source_refs.notes: Used for kickboxing discipline context and legal technique differences.

technical_principles.summary: Every punch or kick must return the athlete to a stance that can defend the next punch, kick, knee, counter, or exit.
Kickboxing combinations should usually finish with a defensive responsibility: guard return, angle exit, distance reset, check readiness, or legal clinch/knee position.
Low-kick and K-1 users need leg-attack and checking systems; point fighters need entry/exit speed and scoring precision; full-contact users need volume, guard, and above-waist kick mechanics.

sport_training_rules.rule: Punch mechanics must preserve stance, guard, and kick-defense readiness; do not teach boxing-only head movement or stance habits that expose knees, kicks, or low kicks.
recommended_action: Use jab, cross, hook, and uppercut mechanics with guard return and stance recovery.
Add kick-defense checks after punching entries for low-kick and K-1 users.

sport_training_rules.rule: Teach kicks with pivot, hip rotation, guarded torso, target control, and recovery to stance before progressing impact, height, or volume.
recommended_action: Start with low or body-height round kicks before repeated head kicks.
Use technical pad or bag volume before hard sparring contact.
blocked_action: hard low-kick exchanges before checking mechanics
spinning attacks before balance and recovery

sport_training_rules.rule: Hard sparring should not be prescribed until the athlete can defend basic punches and kicks, keep balance under contact, and exit safely.
recommended_action: Use technical sparring, partner feeds, defensive drills, and controlled counters first.
Assess guard return, check mechanics, and calm reset under pressure.

planning_rules.rule: A kickboxing technical session should connect warm-up movement, isolated strike mechanics, combination work, defensive response, and exit/reset practice.
recommended_action: Pair offensive combinations with checks, guard returns, or angle exits.
Keep high-speed work low fatigue and high quality.
blocked_action: random bag rounds without technical focus
conditioning circuits that erase guard and stance quality

planning_rules.rule: Low-kick and K-1 athletes should learn low-kick setup, checking, withdrawal, and countering before hard leg-contact volume.
recommended_action: Use shadow, pad, shield, and low-contact partner check drills before sparring volume.
Progress contact gradually based on shin, knee, hip, and ankle tolerance.
blocked_action: low kicks with unresolved knee or ankle pain

teaching_progressions.learning_goal: Build a basic punch-to-kick chain while preserving stance, guard, and exit.
progression_steps: Add rear round kick after cross with controlled balance.
Add partner/pad cue for defensive check or exit.
Use light technical sparring only after stance recovery is reliable.
progression_signals: athlete can reset or angle out on cue

teaching_progressions.learning_goal: Turn low-kick defense into a safe countering opportunity.
progression_steps: Solo check mechanics with posture and guard.
Partner low-contact low-kick feed to check.
Check then return cross or low kick.
progression_signals: no knee or shin pain escalation

sport_skill_assessments.summary: Assess whether the athlete can throw basic punches and round kicks while returning to stance and guard.
metrics: ability to reset stance on coach cue
no pain escalation with technical volume
hold_if: knee, hip, ankle, or shin pain worsens

minimum_evidence: basic punch and kick mechanics are stable
can defend/check basic attacks in partner drills
promote_when: athlete keeps stance and guard under moderate fatigue
athlete can combine attack, defense, and exit
coach/user feedback reports controlled contact readiness
hold_when: hard contact anxiety or unsafe reactions
head, wrist, shoulder, hip, knee, ankle, or shin symptoms worsen
sport_level_transition_rules.backend_action: Unlock simple sparring constraints, counter drills, rule-set-specific combinations, and moderate-intensity round conditioning.
